extracted.intended_audience: researchers (authors and reviewers), especially Wellcome-funded or Wellcome Open Research contributors and readers interested in peer review transparency
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rationale for running an open, post-publication peer review process (Wellcome Open Research model), including reviewer suitability checks, conflict-of-interest declaration and publication, and measures to build trust and encourage reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open and transparent post-publication peer review model
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome Open Research operates an open and transparent post-publication peer review process, where the peer-review process takes place after an article has already been published, and all peer-review reports provided by our reviewers are published online alongside the article so that they are fully visible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This model differs from the traditional model: reviewer names, affiliations and conflicts of interest are published alongside the article (not hidden). Transparent publication of reports promotes a constructive peer-review process, encourages readers to contribute (e.g., by leaving comments on the article and/or the peer-review reports), and allows all readers to track the progress and status of the article in real time. The system is described as being built on a foundation of trust and increasing confidence in the quality of published work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author-led reviewer suggestion
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are allowed to suggest their own reviewers as part of an author-led approach to peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are expected to know their fields and to make ethical choices when suggesting reviewers; the editorial team still conducts checks on suggested reviewers to ensure suitability and absence of conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer qualifications (minimum experience)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should hold a PhD (or an MD) in a relevant field and have published at least 3 articles on the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are baseline expectations but applied on a case-by-case basis — some fields do not require PhDs, and widely published current researchers may be acceptable substitutes. The aim is to ensure reviewers can provide a current, in-depth and knowledgeable review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer independence / no institutional or collaborative association
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should not be associated with any of the authors of the paper, for example by working at the same institution or by having recently published papers together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial team checks for institutional overlap and recent collaborations. Reviewers are also asked to declare other potential conflicts (e.g., friendships or funding relationships) so the team can assess whether they can provide an unbiased review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global spread of reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Every article should obtain a global spread of reviewers to reduce country-to-country bias and gain an international perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensuring geographic diversity of reviewers is an explicit editorial goal to reduce bias and bring broader perspectives to the assessment of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration and publication of competing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: All competing interests for authors and reviewers should be declared and published alongside the peer review reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competing interests are considered to include both financial (e.g., software owned by the reviewer that is used in the article) and non-financial (e.g., recent working relationships with the authors). Publishing competing interest statements together with fully published, citable peer review reports is presented as beneficial to scholarly publishing and increases trust in the peer review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial checks and reviewer suitability screening
rubrics_metrics.description: The editorial team carries out thorough checks on peer review suggestions to ensure reviewers are qualified, experts in the relevant field, and have no conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a list of Reviewer Suitability Checks that all must adhere to; editors assess qualifications and potential conflicts, and ensure reviewers can provide informed feedback, which in turn helps articles obtain the best feedback possible and be indexed efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation and correction of undeclared competing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reader reports an undeclared competing interest, the editorial team will investigate the allegation and, if necessary, highlight the undeclared interest on the peer review reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such situations are described as rare; the system relies on reviewer honesty but retains processes to investigate and correct when trust is misplaced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency to promote constructive review and reader engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Making peer review reports and competing interest statements public promotes constructive peer-review interactions and encourages additional reader contributions (comments and critiques).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open availability of validations, critiques, and reviewer statements gives readers insights often not afforded under traditional models, enabling ongoing discussion between authors, reviewers and the wider community and supporting trust in the process.
